title: Column update metadata representation
summary: Gábor Kaszab opened a discussion on how column files are represented in V4 manifest metadata. The agreed starting point was a ColumnFile struct with field_ids, location and file_size_in_bytes; the open part was tracking information such as sequence numbers and per-column-file status. Steven Wu objected to repurposing file_sequence_number and proposed a separate latest_column_file_sequence_number in the tracking struct. Later updates dropped per-column-file status in favour of change detection through REPLACED and MODIFIED entries of the TrackedFile, and a V4 AMT sync decided to bump the TrackedFile data sequence number instead of adding a new sequence number field. Whether the base file should itself be listed as a column file was debated across several syncs. The final message reports the conclusion to keep the base file separate from column files, and an extended ColumnFile struct with format_version, file_format, key_metadata and split_offsets. The metadata PR was still awaiting review.

positions.stance: Proposed per-column-file status values (EXISTING, ADDED, DELETED, REPLACED) and argued a column-file-level sequence number is not needed for _last_updated_sequence_number.
Do not change the semantics of file_sequence_number; add a latest_column_file_sequence_number field in the tracking struct instead.
After talking with Amogh, per-column-file status, sequence numbers and snapshot IDs are unnecessary; changes are detected by matching REPLACED and MODIFIED TrackedFile entries.
Leans toward keeping base file fields on TrackedFile rather than moving them into the column file list, to match the base file plus column files mental model.

outcome.note: The column update sync concluded to keep the base file separate from column files and extended the ColumnFile struct with format_version, file_format, key_metadata and split_offsets. The metadata PR (#16285) was still open for review.

why_it_matters: It settles the manifest-level structs that V4 column update implementations build on, including that a TrackedFile stays a physical base file with column files on top.
